## Overview Keep MRV2 DBO on its FULL microbatched CUDA graph when a DP rank's real decode tokens don't reach every captured microbatch region. An alternative to #63556 (row staging) and #57020 (eager fallback at the boundary). **Draft: not yet validated end to end** (see Validation). ## Claims - Under FULL, each microbatch keeps the request rows its graph region was captured with. A region with no real tokens replays as ordinary graph padding: query length 0, seq_len 0, slot −1. - DP no longer drops to eager microbatching when one rank's last microbatch is empty. For example, loads 63/97 at bucket 128 replay FULL on both ranks. - No rows are reordered, so there is no output gather or input restore. The production diff is +32/−6, confined to `gpu/ubatch_utils.py` and `gpu/dp_utils.py`. ## Validation Unit tests (1×B300): `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py` gives **31 passed**. The three changed or new tests below fail on `main` and pass with this change: | Test | Checks | | --- | --- | | `test_full_graph_replay_keeps_the_captured_split` | FULL request slices match capture for 16/9/8/4 real requests (eager still clamps) | | `test_full_graph_all_padding_microbatch_is_graph_padding` | The all-padding microbatch has the captured row count, zero query/seq lens and `max_query_len` 1 | | `test_microbatched_graph_survives_a_rank_that_cannot_reach_the_split` | Loads `[33, 128]` now dispatch FULL with 2 microbatches instead of eager | ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py ``` **Not yet done:** - **E2E model run.** The directed DP2/EP2 test from #63556 (`test_mrv2_imbalanced_decode_keeps_full_graph`: DeepSeek-V2-Lite, NIXL EP, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA`, 63/97 at bucket 128, logprobs compared against eager DBO) has not been run. It needs Hopper. - **Throughput A/B** against #63556 and against eager fallback. - **`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` run.** The change adds only host-side slice arithmetic. ## Details **Root cause.** `create_ubatch_slices` clamps a trailing all-padding microbatch's request slice onto the last real request, which keeps eager metadata non-degenerate. Under FULL, that gives the region more request rows than it was captured with: 66 instead of 64 for 63 real tokens at bucket 128. Every row is then offset by two requests. A partially filled non-last region (k > 2, or region 0 when real tokens < split) is similarly short. The DP gate in `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` avoided this by forcing eager. #57020 tightens that gate's boundary. **Change.** FULL microbatch graphs only exist for uniform decodes (`_maybe_ubatch_twin`). Under FULL, the request slice for every region is `token_slice // tokens_per_req`, which is exactly the capture layout, and the eager gate is removed. Padding requests already carry query length 0 and seq_len 0 from `prepare_inputs`, the same as padding rows in a normal FULL graph. The only new case is a region with *no* real rows. For that region, `_slice_input_batch` sets `max_query_len` to the captured uniform length, so `prepare_attn` does not call `.max()` on an empty array. Eager and PIECEWISE microbatching are unchanged. **Compared with #63556.** Replay cost is fixed by the captured shape, so spreading real rows across regions does not reduce graph work. This change gets the same FULL-instead-of-eager benefit without staging, restoration or a capability vote. Under EP, the light rank's padding region still runs expert work for tokens routed from other ranks, so the DBO overlap structure is preserved. **Risks / reviewer attention.** - Every attention backend used with FULL microbatched graphs must tolerate a region whose rows all have seq_len 0, with `max_seq_len` 0 at build time. For FA3 (`FLASH_ATTN_MLA`), `get_scheduler_metadata` gives `num_n_blocks = 0` and so 1 split, and zero query lengths should schedule no tiles; that comes from reading the source, not from testing it. FlashMLA, FlashInfer MLA, CUTLASS MLA and Triton MLA are unverified. - Assumes split points are multiples of the uniform query length (asserted). DBO currently excludes speculative decoding, so this is 1 in practice. ---

Hi @LucasWilkinson, thanks for exploring this alternative! The approach looks promising.

I can help run E2E correctness tests on H200s and benchmark #63823 against #63556 under identical workloads, including DP imbalance and FULL CUDA Graph replay.

I'd be happy to compare correctness, throughput, and latency to see which approach works better in practice.
I'll be completely transparent and objective with the results, regardless of which approach performs better. My goal is to find the best solution for vLLM, not to get my own PR merged.

Hi @LucasWilkinson, I have read your code carefully. Your approach matches my initial idea: **the simplest and most direct solution is to let an empty microbatch run entirely as padding, keeping the captured layout and FULL CUDA Graph replay.** For context, my original staging prototype is [#57184](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57184).

I initially chose staging because I was unsure whether padding-related metadata, KV updates, EP participation, and post-forward bookkeeping stayed consistent when a microbatch became entirely padding. Reading your code now, I see several existing protections:

- **Stale metadata after active → padding transitions:** the [FA3 MLA builder](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/blob/77d369994150a28054c50e7b6ee1fdbd59ea0bf0/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashattn_mla.py#L250-L263) copies the new scheduler metadata and explicitly clears the unused tail. This appears to address my original stale-tail concern.
- **Padding slots accidentally writing KV:** the [MLA KV-update kernel](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/blob/77d369994150a28054c50e7b6ee1fdbd59ea0bf0/csrc/cache_kernels.cu#L529-L550) immediately returns for negative slots, protecting this kernel's `slot_mapping=-1` path.
- **Unwritten padding outputs reaching real tokens:** padding outputs need not be zero if they remain isolated. The default [fused top-k path](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/blob/77d369994150a28054c50e7b6ee1fdbd59ea0bf0/csrc/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu#L550-L565) assigns padding expert IDs of `-1`; the relevant end-to-end check is that the mask reaches the actual routing path.
- **A locally empty microbatch skipping necessary EP work:** it can still receive real expert inputs from other ranks. Your [forward contexts](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/blob/77d369994150a28054c50e7b6ee1fdbd59ea0bf0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/ubatch_utils.py#L425-L455) use padded slice capacity for DP metadata, and I do not see this change introducing a local-empty shortcut that skips EP.

These explain my original caution; I have not measured a failure of your current implementation. I would still exercise repeated active → padding → active transitions, 63/64/65-token boundaries and rank-load swaps with real attention + NIXL + FULL replay, checking real requests' logits/KV and history.

**Avoiding reordering is a real advantage of your approach.** My early staging implementation introduced genuine sampling-position and returned-route bugs because restoring model outputs alone did not restore everything their consumers read. Those were problems in my implementation, not evidence against padding-only replay. I have included the details below, along with the separate numerical and performance findings.

<details>
<summary>Additional context from my staging experiments</summary>

**Sampling positions and returned routes.** Staging rewrote input IDs and positions in place. I restored outputs but initially left the sampler reading staged input buffers through the original logical `logits_indices`. With 63 tokens distributed as 32+31 in a 128-row graph, some logical rows pointed into padding: one recorded position was 146 but the sampler read 0. With the same logits, seed and sampling settings, correcting the logical inputs changed sampled tokens. DP2/DP4 shadow observations recorded 21/19 differences; repeating the original inputs produced zero. The position-dependent `min_tokens` mask was also affected.

Routing needed two separate fixes: restoring logical slot order (one 63-token observation had 31 slots of `-1` in the logical prefix), and using physical microbatch offsets so DBO capture callbacks did not overwrite the same buffer prefix. I restored inputs/positions/slots before post-forward consumers and restored route order after offset-aware writes. A later campaign completed 5,124 requests with the recorded sampling/routing checks passing; this was not an independent oracle for every returned token. The independent capture-offset fix is already in your base through `dbo_current_ubatch_token_offset()`.

**NIXL with `k>2`.** In my later extension, the installed low-latency implementation reused two receive buffers. Extending the handles array alone did not preserve activations, expert counts, optional scales and combine-handle tensors until use. Aliased-snapshot negative controls detected corruption for `k=3/4/8`, while `k=2` was unaffected; FP8 coverage used mock tuples. This is outside your current two-microbatch change, and staging itself did not solve ownership either.

**BF16 and layout effects.** Earlier DeepSeek BF16 tests showed compact-versus-fixed-layout differences even in the unmodified baseline, while same-layout FULL/eager matched. Computing all 26 shared-expert down projections in FP32 before capture removed the observed differences in those campaigns. This supported a shape-dependent numerical contribution in those samples, not a BF16 kernel bug or qualification of the original BF16 path.

**DBO performance.** Early comparisons were eager fallback versus staging + FULL. Later, a no-profiler, two-round DeepSeek-V2-Lite BF16 DP8/EP8 H200 experiment compared DBO ON with ordinary DBO-OFF FULL: NIXL + batched Triton, loads `[63,97,80,80,80,80,80,80]`, bucket 128, budget 8192. Aggregate throughput was 9,836.63 tok/s ON versus 16,497.16 OFF. Retaining FULL therefore did not guarantee a net DBO gain in that workload.

These are historical figures from archived reports, not new GPU runs or independently reprocessed raw data for this comment. They are neither a padding-only-versus-staging comparison nor measurements of your current head. They motivate separating replay correctness, layout-dependent numerical effects and matched performance comparisons.

</details>

My original choice reflected uncertainty about the padding contract, rather than proof that padding-only replay fails. Your approach removes complexity my workaround needed. If the end-to-end checks pass, I would favor its simpler data flow, and compare padding-only FULL, staging FULL and eager fallback under matched conditions.

I am still learning this part of the implementation, so I am concerned that I may have missed something or misunderstood some details. Please correct me if any of the reasoning above is off.

@specture724, since you implemented MRV2 FULL-graph DBO, could you weigh in on the intended contract for an all-padding microbatch? My original #57184 used staging to keep each microbatch nonempty. If the supported backends handle all-padding regions correctly, Lucas's approach seems simpler to me. Is there any DBO-specific constraint that would still require staging? I can help with matched end-to-end validation.

@LucasWilkinson, the small follow-up is now ready for review in the upstream repository: [vllm-project/vllm#64086](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64086). I initially opened [LucasWilkinson/vllm#5](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/pull/5) against the wrong repository and have closed it. The two-file diff is identical; the replacement independently targets `main` and is related to #63823.

It preserves `-1` in NIXL's global-to-physical mapping, which is shared by dispatch and combine, and adds adapter contract tests. The trigger requires both an active mapping table and incoming invalid IDs; I have not established a default-model reproducer.

To clarify how the two changes could work together: `-1` is an invalid/padding route sentinel, not a valid expert ID. If padding-only replay in #63823 sends `-1` routes into NIXL with a non-None global-to-physical mapping table, the existing `mapping[-1]` lookup turns those padding routes into the last real expert in the table. #64086 preserves `-1` through that mapping in both dispatch and combine, so the invalid route stays marked invalid. The changes are complementary, but #64086 fixes an existing adapter behavior on `main` and has no code dependency on #63823. I have not verified that #63823 actually reaches this combination in an end-to-end model run, so I am not claiming that #63823 requires this fix.

The contributed CPU regressions give **2 failed / 1 passed without the fix, and 3 passed with it**. A subsequent H200-host component run passed 36 cases, but the separate native NIXL diagnostic terminated with SIGSEGV and the model stage was not reached; the full job failed. Native transport/model correctness and serving frequency remain unestablished. I'd appreciate your thoughts on whether this defensive adapter fix would be useful alongside #63823.

On merge timing for #64086: I plan to complete an end-to-end H200 comparison of row staging (#63556) versus all-padding replay (#63823) under matched workloads, checking both performance and correctness. If all-padding replay performs better and no correctness issues are observed in those runs, I would suggest considering #64086 for merge alongside that approach, with the mapped `-1` path validated as part of the testing. Alternatively, if you independently confirm that another real workload sends invalid/padding IDs through an active NIXL global-to-physical mapping table and encounters this issue, I would also recommend merging #64086 on that evidence, without waiting for my staging-versus-padding comparison.

cc @bnellnm, as a code owner for the affected fused-MoE adapter and MoE tests in #64086.

@LucasWilkinson, I completed a directed H200 comparison of staging and all-padding replay. In the empty-region case, all-padding replay was slightly faster in all three paired trials. The strict output-equivalence checks remain unresolved.

**Scope:** the measured source was #63556 at `b6660643fbd0514faa08bfcdb7d29bbac1b57ac9`. The padding arm was a local experimental helper on that same source: contiguous real rows, no scatter/gather/restore, captured region capacities, zero query/sequence lengths and slot `-1` for padding. It retained the existing eligibility vote and NIXL capacity. **This was not a run of #63823 at `77d369994150a28054c50e7b6ee1fdbd59ea0bf0`**, so these results compare the mechanisms on a common source rather than validate this PR's exact implementation.

Same two H200s throughout; DeepSeek-V2-Lite revision `604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0`, BF16 weights/KV, DP2/EP2/TP1, NIXL EP, batched_triton, FLASH_ATTN_MLA, MRV2, DBO enabled, two microbatches, FULL bucket `[128]`. Prefix caching and async scheduling were disabled; token budget 8192, max sequences 128/rank, 4 GiB KV/rank. Runtime: Torch 2.13.0+cu129, NIXL 1.5.0.

Each request had a unique synthetic 128-token prompt and exactly 512 output tokens, greedy with EOS ignored. The only loads were **63/97** (rank 0: staging 32/31 versus padding 63/0) and **65/97** (both 64/1, so the second region has one real token and neither arm stages). No balanced-load or DBO-off comparison was included. Eager DBO was used only as a correctness reference.

| Load | Arm | Output tok/s, mean ± sample SD | TPOT p95 ms | HTTP TTFT p95 ms | E2E p95 s |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 63/97 | Staging | 1336.44 ± 2.40 | 118.739 | 1510.76 | 62.012 |
| 63/97 | All padding | 1360.56 ± 8.80 | 117.209 | 1509.57 | 60.804 |
| 65/97 | Staging | 1378.17 ± 9.72 | 116.852 | 1546.79 | 60.802 |
| 65/97 | All padding | 1370.12 ± 1.69 | 117.190 | 1385.43 | 60.919 |

Three paired trials, after warmup, with launch order staging/padding, padding/staging, staging/padding. Percentiles pool 480 or 486 requests per arm. At 63/97, staging's paired throughput changes were −2.35%, −1.28%, −1.68%: mean **−1.77%**, paired 95% t interval [−3.12%, −0.42%]. The 65/97 control was +0.59%, interval [−0.92%, +2.10%]. There are only three independent trial pairs.

Requests were admitted while paused, then resumed together to construct the load. HTTP TTFT includes that intentional admission wait. At 63/97, resume-to-first-token means were essentially identical: 725.24 ms staging and 725.14 ms padding. Throughput uses total output tokens / whole-cohort duration from resume. All 12 performance cohorts recorded **510 actual FULL128/two-microbatch decode replays per rank**, including the expected 32/31, 63/0 or 64/1 layouts. Performance used identical CPU counters and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`; synchronous routing tensor audits were disabled.

**Correctness:** all 1,932 performance requests and 1,932 separate correctness requests completed, but request completion is not an equivalence pass.

- The independent audit covered all 639 model-input positions/request (128 prompt + 511 decode inputs), all 26 MoE layers and six experts/token: 32,098,248 token×layer records. Selected experts satisfied the actual top-6 logits; non-renormalized softmax weights, logical input/slot correspondence and restoration, dispatch mapping and padding sentinels passed. There were zero mismatches across 20,437,248 paired receive-count cells. Six drain forwards lacked a peer snapshot and were excluded from that paired count check. Placement was linear, with no active remapping table; this does not exercise #64086's mapped-sentinel trigger or establish per-activation transport identity.
- Staging versus padding free generation matched all 512 output tokens for **153/160** requests at 63/97 and **161/162** at 65/97.
- On identical prefixes supplied through native trace replay, the expert sets differed in **9.13% / 3.10%** of token×layer records, respectively. Forced-token logprob differences exceeded the preset absolute tolerance 0.1 at **16 / 10** output positions; the maximum was 0.250703. The largest aligned same-set expert-weight difference at 63/97 was 0.694194.
- Eager's own free/trace repeated-prefix reference also exceeded the same logprob tolerance at **5 / 7** positions, and the 65/97 arms execute the same non-staging path. Root cause is unresolved; these observations do not isolate a bug in either approach. Output differences also occurred in the performance runs without routing tensor copies.

Thus, all-padding replay kept FULL and was slightly faster in this directed MLA/NIXL setup, but **strict end-to-end equivalence has not been established**. The synthetic prompts measure consistency, not task answer accuracy.

I am now working on a follow-up **GSM8K answer-accuracy evaluation against the ground-truth answers**, using the same model and the two directed DP cases. It is now queued, awaiting a two-H200 allocation; there are no GSM8K results yet. I will report answer accuracy separately from token/logprob and routing consistency.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @LucasWilkinson.

Hi @LucasWilkinson  , thanks for driving the new approach!

I originally raised this issue in #63556 and have since actively participated in the technical discussions and provided end-to-end validation that helped evaluate the proposed approaches.

I also identified and worked on two related MoE communication correctness issues in the NIXL and DeepEP LL paths:
- #64086 — Preserve invalid expert IDs in NIXL mapping
- #64340 — Preserve invalid expert IDs in DeepEP LL mapping

Given these contributions, would you be open to considering adding me as a co-author of the final implementation, if you feel it's appropriate?

I'm also happy to help with any additional testing or implementation work. Thanks again for your time and consideration!

@@ -414,6 +414,29 @@ def test_all_padding_microbatch_has_no_work_to_do():
     )
 
 
+def test_full_graph_all_padding_microbatch_is_graph_padding():
+    """Under FULL, the microbatch past the last real token holds only padding
+    requests: the captured row count, each with no query and no context."""
+    query_lens, seq_lens = [1] * 6, [64] * 6
+    buffers = _make_buffers()
+    input_batch = _make_input_batch(
+        query_lens, seq_lens, buffers, num_reqs_padded=16, num_tokens_padded=16
+    )
+    ubatch_slices = create_ubatch_slices(input_batch, 2, CUDAGraphMode.FULL)
+    ubatch_buffers = _make_ubatch_buffers()
+
+    first = _slice_input_batch(input_batch, ubatch_slices[0], *ubatch_buffers[0])
+    last = _slice_input_batch(input_batch, ubatch_slices[1], *ubatch_buffers[1])
+
+    assert (first.num_reqs, first.num_reqs_after_padding) == (6, 8)
+    assert (last.num_reqs, last.num_tokens) == (0, 0)
+    assert (last.num_reqs_after_padding, last.num_tokens_after_padding) == (8, 8)
+    assert last.max_query_len == 1
+    assert last.query_start_loc.tolist() == [0] * 9
+    assert last.seq_lens.tolist() == [0] * 8
+    assert last.seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound.tolist() == [0] * 8
+
+
 def test_microbatching_off_when_a_rank_does_not_allow_it():
     assert _sync_dp([256, 256], allow_ubatching=False)[0].num_ubatches == 1

+) -> list[slice]:

Hi @LucasWilkinson, thanks for exploring this alternative! The approach looks promising.

I can help run E2E correctness tests on H200s and benchmark #63823 against #63556 under identical workloads, including DP imbalance and FULL CUDA Graph replay.

I'd be happy to compare correctness, throughput, and latency to see which approach works better in practice.
I'll be completely transparent and objective with the results, regardless of which approach performs better. My goal is to find the best solution for vLLM, not to get my own PR merged.

Hi @LucasWilkinson, I have read your code carefully. Your approach matches my initial idea: **the simplest and most direct solution is to let an empty microbatch run entirely as padding, keeping the captured layout and FULL CUDA Graph replay.** For context, my original staging prototype is [#57184](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57184).

I initially chose staging because I was unsure whether padding-related metadata, KV updates, EP participation, and post-forward bookkeeping stayed consistent when a microbatch became entirely padding. Reading your code now, I see several existing protections:

- **Stale metadata after active → padding transitions:** the [FA3 MLA builder](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/blob/77d369994150a28054c50e7b6ee1fdbd59ea0bf0/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashattn_mla.py#L250-L263) copies the new scheduler metadata and explicitly clears the unused tail. This appears to address my original stale-tail concern.
- **Padding slots accidentally writing KV:** the [MLA KV-update kernel](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/blob/77d369994150a28054c50e7b6ee1fdbd59ea0bf0/csrc/cache_kernels.cu#L529-L550) immediately returns for negative slots, protecting this kernel's `slot_mapping=-1` path.
- **Unwritten padding outputs reaching real tokens:** padding outputs need not be zero if they remain isolated. The default [fused top-k path](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/blob/77d369994150a28054c50e7b6ee1fdbd59ea0bf0/csrc/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu#L550-L565) assigns padding expert IDs of `-1`; the relevant end-to-end check is that the mask reaches the actual routing path.
- **A locally empty microbatch skipping necessary EP work:** it can still receive real expert inputs from other ranks. Your [forward contexts](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/blob/77d369994150a28054c50e7b6ee1fdbd59ea0bf0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/ubatch_utils.py#L425-L455) use padded slice capacity for DP metadata, and I do not see this change introducing a local-empty shortcut that skips EP.

These explain my original caution; I have not measured a failure of your current implementation. I would still exercise repeated active → padding → active transitions, 63/64/65-token boundaries and rank-load swaps with real attention + NIXL + FULL replay, checking real requests' logits/KV and history.

**Avoiding reordering is a real advantage of your approach.** My early staging implementation introduced genuine sampling-position and returned-route bugs because restoring model outputs alone did not restore everything their consumers read. Those were problems in my implementation, not evidence against padding-only replay. I have included the details below, along with the separate numerical and performance findings.

<details>
<summary>Additional context from my staging experiments</summary>

**Sampling positions and returned routes.** Staging rewrote input IDs and positions in place. I restored outputs but initially left the sampler reading staged input buffers through the original logical `logits_indices`. With 63 tokens distributed as 32+31 in a 128-row graph, some logical rows pointed into padding: one recorded position was 146 but the sampler read 0. With the same logits, seed and sampling settings, correcting the logical inputs changed sampled tokens. DP2/DP4 shadow observations recorded 21/19 differences; repeating the original inputs produced zero. The position-dependent `min_tokens` mask was also affected.

Routing needed two separate fixes: restoring logical slot order (one 63-token observation had 31 slots of `-1` in the logical prefix), and using physical microbatch offsets so DBO capture callbacks did not overwrite the same buffer prefix. I restored inputs/positions/slots before post-forward consumers and restored route order after offset-aware writes. A later campaign completed 5,124 requests with the recorded sampling/routing checks passing; this was not an independent oracle for every returned token. The independent capture-offset fix is already in your base through `dbo_current_ubatch_token_offset()`.

**NIXL with `k>2`.** In my later extension, the installed low-latency implementation reused two receive buffers. Extending the handles array alone did not preserve activations, expert counts, optional scales and combine-handle tensors until use. Aliased-snapshot negative controls detected corruption for `k=3/4/8`, while `k=2` was unaffected; FP8 coverage used mock tuples. This is outside your current two-microbatch change, and staging itself did not solve ownership either.

**BF16 and layout effects.** Earlier DeepSeek BF16 tests showed compact-versus-fixed-layout differences even in the unmodified baseline, while same-layout FULL/eager matched. Computing all 26 shared-expert down projections in FP32 before capture removed the observed differences in those campaigns. This supported a shape-dependent numerical contribution in those samples, not a BF16 kernel bug or qualification of the original BF16 path.

**DBO performance.** Early comparisons were eager fallback versus staging + FULL. Later, a no-profiler, two-round DeepSeek-V2-Lite BF16 DP8/EP8 H200 experiment compared DBO ON with ordinary DBO-OFF FULL: NIXL + batched Triton, loads `[63,97,80,80,80,80,80,80]`, bucket 128, budget 8192. Aggregate throughput was 9,836.63 tok/s ON versus 16,497.16 OFF. Retaining FULL therefore did not guarantee a net DBO gain in that workload.

These are historical figures from archived reports, not new GPU runs or independently reprocessed raw data for this comment. They are neither a padding-only-versus-staging comparison nor measurements of your current head. They motivate separating replay correctness, layout-dependent numerical effects and matched performance comparisons.

</details>

My original choice reflected uncertainty about the padding contract, rather than proof that padding-only replay fails. Your approach removes complexity my workaround needed. If the end-to-end checks pass, I would favor its simpler data flow, and compare padding-only FULL, staging FULL and eager fallback under matched conditions.

I am still learning this part of the implementation, so I am concerned that I may have missed something or misunderstood some details. Please correct me if any of the reasoning above is off.

@specture724, since you implemented MRV2 FULL-graph DBO, could you weigh in on the intended contract for an all-padding microbatch? My original #57184 used staging to keep each microbatch nonempty. If the supported backends handle all-padding regions correctly, Lucas's approach seems simpler to me. Is there any DBO-specific constraint that would still require staging? I can help with matched end-to-end validation.

@LucasWilkinson, the small follow-up is now ready for review in the upstream repository: [vllm-project/vllm#64086](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64086). I initially opened [LucasWilkinson/vllm#5](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/pull/5) against the wrong repository and have closed it. The two-file diff is identical; the replacement independently targets `main` and is related to #63823.

It preserves `-1` in NIXL's global-to-physical mapping, which is shared by dispatch and combine, and adds adapter contract tests. The trigger requires both an active mapping table and incoming invalid IDs; I have not established a default-model reproducer.

To clarify how the two changes could work together: `-1` is an invalid/padding route sentinel, not a valid expert ID. If padding-only replay in #63823 sends `-1` routes into NIXL with a non-None global-to-physical mapping table, the existing `mapping[-1]` lookup turns those padding routes into the last real expert in the table. #64086 preserves `-1` through that mapping in both dispatch and combine, so the invalid route stays marked invalid. The changes are complementary, but #64086 fixes an existing adapter behavior on `main` and has no code dependency on #63823. I have not verified that #63823 actually reaches this combination in an end-to-end model run, so I am not claiming that #63823 requires this fix.

The contributed CPU regressions give **2 failed / 1 passed without the fix, and 3 passed with it**. A subsequent H200-host component run passed 36 cases, but the separate native NIXL diagnostic terminated with SIGSEGV and the model stage was not reached; the full job failed. Native transport/model correctness and serving frequency remain unestablished. I'd appreciate your thoughts on whether this defensive adapter fix would be useful alongside #63823.

On merge timing for #64086: I plan to complete an end-to-end H200 comparison of row staging (#63556) versus all-padding replay (#63823) under matched workloads, checking both performance and correctness. If all-padding replay performs better and no correctness issues are observed in those runs, I would suggest considering #64086 for merge alongside that approach, with the mapped `-1` path validated as part of the testing. Alternatively, if you independently confirm that another real workload sends invalid/padding IDs through an active NIXL global-to-physical mapping table and encounters this issue, I would also recommend merging #64086 on that evidence, without waiting for my staging-versus-padding comparison.

cc @bnellnm, as a code owner for the affected fused-MoE adapter and MoE tests in #64086.

@LucasWilkinson, I completed a directed H200 comparison of staging and all-padding replay. In the empty-region case, all-padding replay was slightly faster in all three paired trials. The strict output-equivalence checks remain unresolved.

**Scope:** the measured source was #63556 at `b6660643fbd0514faa08bfcdb7d29bbac1b57ac9`. The padding arm was a local experimental helper on that same source: contiguous real rows, no scatter/gather/restore, captured region capacities, zero query/sequence lengths and slot `-1` for padding. It retained the existing eligibility vote and NIXL capacity. **This was not a run of #63823 at `77d369994150a28054c50e7b6ee1fdbd59ea0bf0`**, so these results compare the mechanisms on a common source rather than validate this PR's exact implementation.

Same two H200s throughout; DeepSeek-V2-Lite revision `604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0`, BF16 weights/KV, DP2/EP2/TP1, NIXL EP, batched_triton, FLASH_ATTN_MLA, MRV2, DBO enabled, two microbatches, FULL bucket `[128]`. Prefix caching and async scheduling were disabled; token budget 8192, max sequences 128/rank, 4 GiB KV/rank. Runtime: Torch 2.13.0+cu129, NIXL 1.5.0.

Each request had a unique synthetic 128-token prompt and exactly 512 output tokens, greedy with EOS ignored. The only loads were **63/97** (rank 0: staging 32/31 versus padding 63/0) and **65/97** (both 64/1, so the second region has one real token and neither arm stages). No balanced-load or DBO-off comparison was included. Eager DBO was used only as a correctness reference.

| Load | Arm | Output tok/s, mean ± sample SD | TPOT p95 ms | HTTP TTFT p95 ms | E2E p95 s |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 63/97 | Staging | 1336.44 ± 2.40 | 118.739 | 1510.76 | 62.012 |
| 63/97 | All padding | 1360.56 ± 8.80 | 117.209 | 1509.57 | 60.804 |
| 65/97 | Staging | 1378.17 ± 9.72 | 116.852 | 1546.79 | 60.802 |
| 65/97 | All padding | 1370.12 ± 1.69 | 117.190 | 1385.43 | 60.919 |

Three paired trials, after warmup, with launch order staging/padding, padding/staging, staging/padding. Percentiles pool 480 or 486 requests per arm. At 63/97, staging's paired throughput changes were −2.35%, −1.28%, −1.68%: mean **−1.77%**, paired 95% t interval [−3.12%, −0.42%]. The 65/97 control was +0.59%, interval [−0.92%, +2.10%]. There are only three independent trial pairs.

Requests were admitted while paused, then resumed together to construct the load. HTTP TTFT includes that intentional admission wait. At 63/97, resume-to-first-token means were essentially identical: 725.24 ms staging and 725.14 ms padding. Throughput uses total output tokens / whole-cohort duration from resume. All 12 performance cohorts recorded **510 actual FULL128/two-microbatch decode replays per rank**, including the expected 32/31, 63/0 or 64/1 layouts. Performance used identical CPU counters and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`; synchronous routing tensor audits were disabled.

**Correctness:** all 1,932 performance requests and 1,932 separate correctness requests completed, but request completion is not an equivalence pass.

- The independent audit covered all 639 model-input positions/request (128 prompt + 511 decode inputs), all 26 MoE layers and six experts/token: 32,098,248 token×layer records. Selected experts satisfied the actual top-6 logits; non-renormalized softmax weights, logical input/slot correspondence and restoration, dispatch mapping and padding sentinels passed. There were zero mismatches across 20,437,248 paired receive-count cells. Six drain forwards lacked a peer snapshot and were excluded from that paired count check. Placement was linear, with no active remapping table; this does not exercise #64086's mapped-sentinel trigger or establish per-activation transport identity.
- Staging versus padding free generation matched all 512 output tokens for **153/160** requests at 63/97 and **161/162** at 65/97.
- On identical prefixes supplied through native trace replay, the expert sets differed in **9.13% / 3.10%** of token×layer records, respectively. Forced-token logprob differences exceeded the preset absolute tolerance 0.1 at **16 / 10** output positions; the maximum was 0.250703. The largest aligned same-set expert-weight difference at 63/97 was 0.694194.
- Eager's own free/trace repeated-prefix reference also exceeded the same logprob tolerance at **5 / 7** positions, and the 65/97 arms execute the same non-staging path. Root cause is unresolved; these observations do not isolate a bug in either approach. Output differences also occurred in the performance runs without routing tensor copies.

Thus, all-padding replay kept FULL and was slightly faster in this directed MLA/NIXL setup, but **strict end-to-end equivalence has not been established**. The synthetic prompts measure consistency, not task answer accuracy.

I am now working on a follow-up **GSM8K answer-accuracy evaluation against the ground-truth answers**, using the same model and the two directed DP cases. It is now queued, awaiting a two-H200 allocation; there are no GSM8K results yet. I will report answer accuracy separately from token/logprob and routing consistency.
